title: Mnemonic Mercenary
user: Players who want a touch-friendly browser roguelike with a fresh run each break, where memory creates tactical tension rather than a reflex test.

evidence.quote_or_summary: The maker describes a browser-and-mobile roguelike built around memorization strings, and an HN commenter asks about the combat/memory mechanic — a concrete 2026 exploration of browser roguelike novelty.
The fetched live game presents a character selection and a memory-limited descent ('How deep can you go before your memory fails?').

recurrence: A browser/mobile roguelike built around a nonstandard input constraint received active discussion, showing appetite beyond generic attack-button action games.
current_workaround: Play word/memory apps without a game arc, or play a conventional roguelike that does not work well in a spare minute on touch.
incumbents_and_gap: Word games train recall and roguelikes provide variation, but they rarely combine a short tactical run with an accessible, low-input memory mechanic. Existing examples can become string-typing tests.
smallest_useful_product: A 10-minute expedition of six fights. Before each fight, a 3-7 symbol route flashes; recalling it selects a tactical stance, while a safe partial recall is always available. Each run changes enemy tells, route length curve, and one relic. Non-goals: speed typing, endless dungeon depth, ads between rooms, or account progression.
success_measure: At least 50% of first-time players finish a run, while returning players choose the harder recall path in 30% of eligible fights.
monetization: one-time — no energy timers or memory-training subscription; sell a complete accessible game.
constraints: Never make color the sole symbol cue; tune for cognitive accessibility with a non-timed mode; local-only save; original icons/audio.
why_distinct: It uses memory as a forgiving tactical choice with a real run ending, not as a naked score-chasing exercise.
